title: Current temperature had a stronger link than prior-year temperature to Northeast Shelf plankton thermal composition in 2004-2022
abstract: We tested thermal memory with NOAA EcoMon tows and OISST beyond BBS and network summaries. Taxon lists and thermal scores were fixed with 1992-2003 records. In 2004-2022, the zooplankton test used 7,364 tows in 409 cell-season units. Joint models included current, past and future SST, local trends and survey-date controls. The current coefficient was 0.0539 (conditional 95% interval 0.0362 to 0.0785). The prior-year coefficient was 0.0039 (-0.0115 to 0.0196). The planned past-minus-future contrast was 0.0060 (-0.0267 to 0.0327). A three-month contrast was also uncertain. In a post-fit comparison, the prior-year/current ratio was 0.073 (-0.191 to 0.364). Fish larvae had a positive current link, an uncertain past link and an unexpected negative future link. All planned time-direction contrast intervals included zero. The data support a current temperature association but do not establish year-scale thermal memory. They do not identify rapid demography or transport as its cause. Conditional score uncertainty, seven time blocks, local detrending, surface exposure and selected catches limit inference. Code, input hashes, aggregate evidence and external-data retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Joint current, past and future SST coefficients and their time-direction contrasts. Thermal scores use 1992-2003; test records use 2004-2022. Bars show conditional 95% crossed-bootstrap intervals. Left: zooplankton. Right: fish larvae. The two exposure horizons are 3 and 12 months.
